steps: Parts & base kit
Included: fire poker and manual kit (warranty cards, catalytic thermometer). One base kit is required: S.Z2613 SC Leg Kit or S.Z3903 Pedestal Kit.

Included: fire poker (it moves fuel and lifts the ash plug with its hook) and the manual kit with warranty cards and catalytic thermometer.

Required, install one: S.Z2613 SC Leg Kit or S.Z3903 Pedestal Kit. Optional: S.Z2514 Fan Kit, S.Z3820 Leg Ash Drawer Kit, S.Z4015 Rear Shield, 3" Outside Air Kit (S.Z1726B), 4" Outside Air Kit (S.Z1726).

Consult the authority having jurisdiction about a permit and installation inspection. Don't install damaged, incomplete or substitute components.
Site & clearances
Freestanding room heater: not in a fireplace or sleeping room, no alcove in Canada. Hold clearances A–J from the p. 9 diagram; flue pipe 6" 24 MSG steel.
Floor protection
Combustible floor: non-combustible floor shield, 16" out front and 8" either side of the loading door (USA), min. 32" × 40.125". Shield under the connector, 2" each side.
Combustion air
Balance intake air in tight homes; a fresh air intake into the room is recommended. An outside air hose must feed up into the rear intake channel.
Mobile home kits
Mobile home only: Outside Air Kit plus a Fan Kit or Rear Shield, best installed before the stove. Double-wall close-clearance pipe, roof exit only, stove fastened to the floor.
Leg or pedestal kit
Lean the stove back with cardboard in the firebox to support the bricks. Legs: 3/4" wrench, level with the leg bolts; pedestal: 7/16" wrench.

SC Leg Kit (S.Z2613) · 3/4" wrench

  1. Lean the stove back onto the main air tube; cardboard inside the firebox supports the bricks.
  2. Position each leg and leg plate (flanges up, away from the leg) parallel to the base edges and fasten with the kit hardware.
  3. Stand the stove upright and level it with the bolts at the bottom of each leg.

Pedestal Kit (S.Z3903) · 7/16" wrench

  1. Lean the stove back (cardboard in the firebox).
  2. Remove the ash channel seal (1/4" nut).
  3. Thread the four 1/4"-20 button head cap screws halfway into the stove base.
  4. Take the ash drawer out of the pedestal (and the rear panel if needed).
  5. Using the key holes on top of the pedestal, push it against the bottom of the stove and slide it downward (stove on its back).
  6. Fully tighten all four fasteners, stand the stove upright and refit the ash drawer.

Either kit must be installed before the stove is connected to the chimney.
Hang the door
The door is heavy: lower it onto the bottom, then top, hinge pins until the hinge surfaces meet. Fit the bypass handle onto the bypass extension on the right side.
Connector & chimney
Stove top adaptor and screwed 6" flue pipe to a UL-103HT or lined masonry chimney, 15 ft minimum vertical. Never share a flue.

Either base kit must be on before the stove is connected to the chimney.

  • Stove top adaptor, then flue pipe (6", 24 MSG steel, single or double wall, inside the room only) to a listed ceiling support package or wall pass-through, then the chimney.
  • Chimney: listed factory-built for solid fuel, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or a code-compliant masonry chimney with flue liner, inspected and cleaned first; Blaze King recommends a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated.
  • Fasten every joint with sheet metal screws; keep the connector as direct as possible; never run flue pipe through an attic, closet, floor or ceiling.
  • Buy all prefab components from the same chimney manufacturer; keep an effective vapor barrier where the chimney penetrates the exterior.
  • Height: 15 ft minimum stove top to termination (0 - 1000 ft); 3 ft above the roof penetration and 2 ft above anything within 10 ft horizontally.
  • Never connect to a chimney serving another appliance (voids the warranty).
Fan kit power
Plug the grounded three-prong cord straight into a grounded receptacle; never cut the ground prong or route the cord in front of or under the stove.
Record & hand over
Complete the installer details on the last page (dealer, installer, date, serial number) and leave the manual with the homeowner.

panels.title: Not enough heat
items: Green or wet wood → check it with a moisture meter
Not enough fuel → load fully; it burns no hotter than the thermostat setting
Thermostat set too low → raise the setting
Combustor plugged, coated or not working → clean, test or replace
Poor draft, wind downdraft or a tight house → manometer check, wind-resistant cap, outside air kit
Too much wood on too few coals → build a larger coal bed

panels.title: Too much heat
items: Bypass door left open → close it
Thermostat set too high → lower the setting
Door gasket leaking → replace the gasket and/or adjust the door
Excessive chimney draft → measure with a manometer; install a cap
Wood too small → use larger pieces
Thermostat not operating properly → Blaze King dealer

panels.title: Smoke spills when loading
items: Spark arrestor screen plugged → clean to bare metal wire
Chimney too cold → use double wall stove pipe
Not enough vertical rise → 36" minimum before elbows; two 45s instead of a 90
Chimney not drafting → thermostat high, bypass open, door closed, wait 5-10 minutes

panels.title: Thermometer won't reach Active
items: Improper operation → check thermostat setting and procedure
Obstruction in chimney or cap → clean the chimney
Faulty thermometer → check its calibration
Wet wood, or combustor plugged / dead → seasoned wood; clean, test or replace
Bypass door leaking → clean around it; adjust or replace the gasket

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Check that all the firebricks are in place and build the fire right on the brick floor. Don't use a grate.

  1. Turn the thermostat to high and the fan (if you have one) off.
  2. Open the bypass, then open the loading door.
  3. Put 10 balls of non-glossy paper toward the front and stack 20 pieces of kindling crisscross on top, with air gaps.
  4. Light it and leave the door cracked open. Stay with the stove.
  5. When the kindling is fully burning, add two or three medium logs. Keep the door unlatched until they catch.
  6. Latch the door. When the combustor temperature starts to climb, close the bypass. Leaving the door open once the wood burns can wear out the combustor early.
  7. When nearly all the wood is burning and the thermometer reads Active, open the bypass and door, fill the stove with wood laid as far back as you can, then latch the door and close the bypass.
  8. Leave it on high until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down gradually.
Note: step 7 on p. 23 says to turn fans on to high as you close the bypass; step 11 on p. 23 says to turn the fan on after the initial warm-up, and p. 19 says to keep fans off until the stove reaches normal operating temperature.
First fire: curing paint gives off a strong smell and smoke, and may change color. Burn at a low setting for several hours with a door or window open.

reload.title: Reloading the stove
reload.html:
Check the catalytic thermometer first. If the needle is still in the Active zone, follow these steps. If it has dropped to Inactive, use the lighting steps instead.

  1. Have the next load of wood ready. Turn the thermostat to high and wait a few minutes.
  2. Open the bypass and wait a few more minutes for the airflow to settle.
  3. Crack the loading door open and give it a minute.
  4. Open the door slowly and load. If smoke spills out, close the door a little to get the draft going again.
  5. Latch the door and close the bypass right away. Leave it on high until the fire is well established, then turn the thermostat down.

On low settings you may see very little flame. That's normal while the needle stays in the Active zone.

Don't be afraid to fill it. The wood only burns at the rate the thermostat is set to, and a glowing bed of coals helps the next load catch.
Mild spring and fall days: run on high for 30 minutes after lighting or reloading, keep the setting high enough that the thermometer stays Active, and burn smaller loads instead of turning the thermostat way down.

controls.title: Thermostat, bypass & fan
controls.html:
Thermostat knob

The knob is at the upper right rear corner of the stove. At high, the stove burns fastest and gives the most heat. Turn it counter clockwise for less heat.

  • Make changes gradually. Turning it too fast can make the thermostat work poorly.
  • Turned down too low, the fire can go out or the combustor can stop working (the thermometer drops to Inactive). Turn it back up and let the fire recover.
  • The lowest setting is fixed at the factory. It's against federal regulations to alter it.

Bypass handle

The handle on the right side works a door inside the top of the stove. Open, it lets smoke skip the catalytic combustor while you light or reload.

  • Pointing forward: bypass open.
  • To close: turn it clockwise until it points to the rear, then push down until you hear a click.

Leaving the bypass open too long can over-fire the stove and build up creosote.

Fan kit: about 30 minutes after the fire is going, set the fan speed to match the thermostat: low with low, medium with medium, high with high.

catalyst.title: The catalytic combustor & thermometer
catalyst.html:
Smoke from the fire passes through a catalytic combustor for a clean burn. The thermometer on top of the stove shows whether it's working. Never run the stove without the combustor.

  • Active zone: above 500F, a clean burn. A healthy combustor often runs above 1000F.
  • Inactive zone: below 500F, not a clean burn.

Switch the fan off for a few minutes before you read it.

Note: p. 21 says to turn the fan off for about 5 minutes before reading the thermometer; p. 32 and p. 38 say 10 minutes.

If it won't go Active

  • Turn the thermostat up, and burn only dry, seasoned wood.
  • Check the chimney and cap for a blockage.
  • A hot fire usually cleans deposits off the combustor best. Otherwise, with the stove cold, lift off the flame shield and brush the combustor face gently with a soft paint brush. Never scrape it.
  • Still Inactive after cleaning? It may need replacing. Call your Blaze King dealer.

Look at the combustor at least three times each heating season. Turning the thermostat down early in a burn can make the combustor temperature climb for up to several hours. That's normal.

wood.title: Choosing wood
wood.html:
Burn natural cord wood only. Hardwood and softwood both burn well; dense hardwood burns a little slower and longer.

  • Aim for 20% moisture or lower: split, stack and cover it from rain and snow for at least 24 months, stacked so air reaches it.
  • Never burn wet, green or unseasoned wood. It wastes heat and can cause excessive creosote build-up, and if that ignites it can cause a chimney fire that may result in a house fire and serious bodily harm.
  • Dimensional timber off-cuts, small very dry pieces and pressed wood logs used in excess can overheat and damage the firebox and combustor.

Check it with a moisture meter

  1. Pick three logs at random and split each one.
  2. Measure each split face 2" from both ends and in the middle, with the pins in line with the grain.
  3. Average all the readings.
Never burn treated wood, coal, charcoal, colored paper, cardboard, garbage or solvents. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes and/or carbon monoxide, which may result in poisoning. Never burn salt-water driftwood or flammable fluids such as gasoline, naphtha or engine gel. Never use chemicals or fluids such as gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene or charcoal lighter fluid to start or freshen up a fire in the stove. Doing so may lead to over-firing, resulting in a house fire and serious bodily harm.

care.title: Ashes & regular care
care.html:
Wait until the fire is out and the stove is cool. The glass and metal stay hot for a long time.

Ashes

  • Empty ashes whenever they come within one inch of the door opening. Leave a bed about 1/2" thick: wood burns best on it.
  • Put them in a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a non-combustible floor or outside on the ground, away from anything that burns, and keep it closed until every cinder is cold. Don't put other waste in it.
Never store hot ashes in a garage or basement. They give off carbon monoxide and flammable gases.

Through the heating season

  • Look over the combustor, and check the thermometer, thermostat and fans.
  • Check that every gasket seals, and have the chimney inspected and cleaned.
  • After the last fire, empty all ash from the firebox and ash drawer and look for warped metal parts.

Door-seal test

With the stove cold, close the door on a dollar bill and pull it out. No resistance means the door needs adjusting; repeat around the door. Don't use the stove with a missing or damaged door gasket. Your dealer can replace it.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
The easiest way to keep the glass clean is to burn hot for a while after each reload. Moisture driven out of fresh wood causes much of the creosote on the glass.

  • Leave the thermostat higher for 30 minutes to an hour before turning it low for an overnight burn.
  • Deposits after long, low burns: run the stove on high for about 30 minutes to burn most of them off.

Cleaning by hand

  • Only when the stove and glass are cool.
  • Use a soft cloth, and no abrasive cleaners.
  • Rinse well with water after any cleaner, or the residue bakes on and is very hard to remove.
Don't strike the glass or slam the door, and don't use the stove if the glass or its gasket is broken. Replacement glass must be 5 mm ceramic glass.
The warranty covers thermal breakage only, not glass that was struck or cleaned with harsh or abrasive cleaners.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires make tar vapors that mix with moisture and condense in the cooler chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot. Hotter fires leave less creosote.

  • Inspect the chimney and flue pipe regularly through the heating season, especially the coldest months, until you know how often it needs cleaning.
  • Have the chimney and stove cleaned at least once a year, or as often as needed. A professional chimney sweep is recommended.
  • Open the bypass before sweeping so soot falls into the firebox.

If a run-away or chimney fire starts

  1. Turn the thermostat knob fully counter clockwise and make sure the loading door and bypass are closed.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Check the chimney, attic and roof for anything hot enough to catch fire. Use an extinguisher or a garden hose if needed.
  4. Afterwards, have a certified chimney sweep inspect the chimney and flue connector. Don't use the stove until you're sure the chimney isn't damaged.

Common causes: the wrong fuel or kindling-size pieces, the door or bypass left open too long, worn gaskets and creosote build-up.

Very cold weather: water vapor can freeze in some exterior chimneys and block them, putting the fire out. Burn on high for 5 to 10 minutes to melt any ice.
Chimney fire damage isn't covered by the warranty.

safety.title: Safety around the stove
safety.html:
• The stove is hot whenever it's running. Keep children and pets from touching it.
  • Keep furniture, clothing and other things that can burn at least 48" from the front. Don't store wood within the clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Run it with the loading door closed, and open it only to add wood. Don't block the air openings or the space under the stove.
  • Never run it without the catalytic combustor and the flame shield in place.
  • Keep at least one smoke detector and one carbon monoxide monitor in the room with the stove, and a fire extinguisher in a central spot everyone knows. Don't switch off or move the detectors.
  • If an alarm sounds, get everyone out first. Fix the cause only once there's no risk.
Make a plan: agree in advance on what everyone does if a chimney fire starts.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Blaze King's limited warranty covers the original purchaser of a stove bought from an authorized dealer, from the date of purchase. It can't be transferred.

Catalytic combustor6 years
Stove body, steel firebox parts5 years
Fans, thermostat, door handle steel parts2 years
All parts and materials, incl. paint1 year

Later years are shared costs. Combustor: no charge for the first three years, then 60%, 70% and 80% of the then-current retail price in years 4, 5 and 6, returned through your dealer with a completed Combustor Failure Report. Parts covered beyond the first year: you pay 20% in year 2, 40% in year 3, 60% in year 4 and 80% in year 5.

Not covered

  • Gaskets and firebrick
  • Over-firing damage (warped plates, burnt-off paint)
  • Glass, except thermal breakage
  • Salt-saturated wood, corrosive driftwood, chemically treated wood or any fuel not recommended
  • Draft or smoke problems caused by surroundings such as trees, wind or hills
Report a problem to your dealer within 30 days of finding it, with proof and date of purchase. This is a summary; the full terms are in the manual.

specEmissions.title: Emissions & heat output
specEmissions.html:
Certified to the U.S. EPA 2020 particulate emission standards using crib wood (EPA test method 28R).

Low burn0.57 g/hr · CO 0.10 g/min
Med-low burn1.09 g/hr · CO 0.64 g/min
Med-high burn0.91 g/hr · CO 0.62 g/min
High burn2.51 g/hr · CO 0.92 g/min
EPA weighted average1.05 g/hr
Heat delivered (test)10,786 – 31,092 Btu/hr
Maker's website: Constant Heat Output on Low 11,370 BTU's/h for up to 20 hours; Constant Heat Output on High 32,776 BTU's/h for up to 8 hours.

Efficiency is determined by the B415.1-10 method and expressed as HHV; the manual prints no efficiency figure.

Maker's website: HHV Tested Efficiency 80.4%.

The manufacturer-set minimum low burn rate must not be altered.

Note: the certification label on p. 4 gives the listing standards as UL 1482-11(R2022) & CAN/ULC-S627:2023; the preface on p. 5 says the stove was tested and listed to CAN/ULC-S628:2022 & UL1482-11 (R2022).

specFlue.title: Flue & chimney type
specFlue.html:
Flue diameter6" (collar 6" I.D.)
Connector6", 24 MSG steel; no aluminum or galvanized
Chimney6" listed factory-built for solid fuel, UL-103HT (USA) / CAN/ULC-S629 (CAN), or code-compliant masonry with flue liner
Close clearance / mobile home6" listed double-wall close-clearance connector with matching listed chimney

Never connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance, or to air distribution ductwork unless specifically approved. Don't install the chimney directly at the outlet; use a connector kept as direct as possible, never through an attic, closet, floor or ceiling. Screw every joint. Use a listed chimney support package through a ceiling and a listed wall thimble through a combustible wall. In a masonry chimney Blaze King recommends a stainless steel liner, preferably insulated. In Canada, follow CSA B365-M87.

specHeight.title: Recommended chimney heights
specHeight.html:
Minimum vertical chimney height, stove top to termination, by elevation and elbows (no more than one offset; two 45° elbows equal one 90°):

Elevation0 · 2 × 15° · 2 × 30° · 2 × 45°
0 - 1000 ft15 · 16 · 18 · 19 ft
1000 - 2000 ft15.5 · 16.5 · 18.5 · 19.5 ft
2000 - 3000 ft16 · 17 · 19 · 20 ft
3000 - 4000 ft16.5 · 17.5 · 19.5 · 20.5 ft
4000 - 5000 ft17 · 18 · 20 · 21 ft
5000 - 6000 ft17.5 · 18.5 · 20.5 · 21.5 ft
6000 - 7000 ft18 · 19 · 21 · 22 ft
7000 - 8000 ft18.5 · 19.5 · 21.5 · 22.5 ft

Add 2.0 ft per 90° elbow, 3.0 ft per "T" section and 2 ft per 1.0 ft of horizontal run (manual's sea-level example: 15.0 + 2.0 + 4.0 + 3.0 = 24.0 ft). Above the roof: at least 3 ft higher than where it passes through the roof and 2 ft higher than any part of the roof or obstruction within 10 ft horizontally (p. 11). Double wall pipe from stove top adaptor to ceiling support box is recommended; for wall exits, 3 ft vertical from stove top to elbow and a pair of 45° elbows rather than one 90°. The figures are guidelines; draft still needs fine tuning.

specClear.title: Clearances to combustibles
specClear.html:
Minimum clearances, roof or wall exit, parallel or corner. Mobile home installs (roof exit only) use the same values and need the Outside Air Kit plus a Fan Kit or Rear Shield Kit.

A12.75"
B6.5"
C *25.25"
D *15.875"
E6"
F *18.5"
J37"

What each letter measures is shown only on the clearance diagram on p. 9 (repeated on the label, p. 4), together with further US / Canada dimensions (G, H, I, K, L); read these values against that drawing. * In Canada, 18" clearance from single wall pipe is required; check local codes and the pipe maker's specs for pipe clearances. Clearances may only be reduced by means approved by the regulatory authority. Keep combustible objects at least 48" from the front (p. 24).

Not to be installed in a fireplace or in a sleeping room. In Canada, not in an alcove; in the USA, keep the minimum clearances.

specFloor.title: Floor protection
specFloor.html:
No thermal hearth pad is required, but on a combustible floor a non-combustible floor shield must be used.

USA, out from the front16"
USA, either side of the loading door8"
Minimum size, USA32" × 40.125"
Minimum size, Canada41" × 50.125"

A non-combustible shield is also required under the chimney connector, extending at least 2" either side of it; the manual says this shield needs no insulation value but must be listed under UL 1618-2009 (Type 1), with a minimum size of 32" x 40.125" in the USA. In Canada (CSA B365), ember protection extends at least 18" on any side with a door and 8" on the other sides. Blaze King doesn't recommend adhesive-based vinyl flooring in front of the stove.

specAir.title: Outside air & mobile home
specAir.html:
In tight homes, balance intake air for every exhausting appliance (HRVs, air handlers, range hoods, dryers); a fresh air intake into the room is recommended (p. 10).

3" Outside Air KitS.Z1726B
4" Outside Air KitS.Z1726
Fan KitS.Z2514
Rear Shield KitS.Z4015 (minimum rear clearances)

The fresh air hose runs through an outside wall or up through the floor, must stay open, and must never penetrate a wall higher than the bottom of the intake air channel on the rear of the stove; it feeds up into that channel.

Mobile home (USA)

  • Outside Air Kit plus a Fan Kit or Rear Shield Kit; installing the kits before the stove is recommended.
  • Flue pipe double wall, close clearance (no single wall); listed UL-103HT chimney; roof exit only. The chimney must be removed to transport the building.
  • Fasten the stove to the floor: Leg Kit with the S.ZR8039 Leg Anchor Kit; Pedestal Kit with #10 screws and washers through the two holes in the base.
  • Not in a sleeping room; keep the structural integrity of the floor, wall and roof.
Note: p. 14 (and pp. 4, 9) call for the Outside Air Kit plus either a Fan Kit or a Rear Shield Kit in a mobile home; p. 15 lists the Rear Shield Kit and the Fan Kit each as required for mobile home or alcove installations.

Two numbers are printed for the combustor: S.CAT203032 is the Blaze King part number for the combustor supplied with the stove (p. 29), listed as the combustor assembly in the parts list (p. 40); Z0336A-M is the combustor OEM part number printed on the certification label (p. 4).

conflicts.issue: Canadian listing standard: the certification label says tested to UL 1482-11(R2022) & CAN/ULC-S627:2023; the preface says tested and listed to CAN/ULC-S628:2022 & UL1482-11 (R2022). Header certification shows only the UL standard both pages agree on.

conflicts.reason: Two numbering systems, not a misprint: Z0336A-M is the combustor OEM part number on the certification label (p. 4); S.CAT203032 is Blaze King's own part number for the supplied combustor (p. 29), the combustor assembly in the parts list (p. 40). The guide shows both, saying what each is.

conflicts.issue: Fan timing at start-up: Lighting the Fire step 7 says turn fans on to high when closing the bypass; step 11 says turn the fan on after the initial warm up; Fan Operation says keep fans off until normal operating temperature (about 30 minutes after the fire is established).
Fan-off time before reading the catalytic thermometer: approximately 5 minutes (p. 21) vs 10 minutes (p. 32 maintenance note; p. 38 troubleshooting).
Mobile-home kits: Outside Air Kit plus either a Fan Kit or a Rear Shield Kit (pp. 4, 9, 14) vs Rear Shield Kit and Fan Kit each described as required for mobile home or alcove installations (p. 15).

catalog_mismatches.manual: No efficiency figure printed; p. 19 gives only the B415.1-10 method and HHV basis

review.notes: The manual prints no efficiency percentage (p. 19 only names the B415.1-10 method and HHV basis), no burn time and no heating area, so the catalog's efficiency, maximum burn time and heating-area figures could not be checked. Flue size 6", 1.05 g/hr emissions, catalytic combustion, optional fan, outside air kits and mobile-home approval match the catalog.
